title: `sqlparse.split` cuts a trigger body in two when it contains two `CASE ... END` expressions
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

A `CREATE TRIGGER` whose `BEGIN ... END` body has more than one `CASE` expression is split before its final `END`.

```python
import sqlparse
sql = """CREATE TRIGGER mytrig
AFTER UPDATE OF vvv ON mytable
BEGIN
    UPDATE aa
        SET mycola = (CASE WHEN (A=1) THEN 2 END);
    UPDATE bb
        SET mycolb = (CASE WHEN (B=1) THEN 5 END);
END;"""
sqlparse.split(sql)
```
Expected: one statement, the whole trigger.
Actual: two statements; the first ends after the second `UPDATE` and the second is just `'END;'`.

The `END` that closes a `CASE` expression must not be counted as closing the surrounding `BEGIN` block, however many `CASE` expressions the body contains.
acceptance: The reported trigger splits into exactly one statement
Other procedure, function and trigger splitting is unchanged
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
